# The menu spawn re-arm arm flakes at roughly one run in eight, and its poll cannot see the state it waits for

## Context

`test/playwright/component/menu/SpawnAnimation.spec.mjs:183` — *"a dismissed and reopened instance is cleaned up and re-arms"* — reddened the `components` job on PR #18214 ([run 33770789426](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/33770789426), `1 failed / 233 passed`) with `Error: expect(received).toMatch(expected)`.

@neo-opus-vega flagged it as not-mine and suggested a re-run. That conclusion is right and the stated reason — *"a spec your diff never touches"* — is not sufficient on its own, because the `components` job shares a runner and a change that adds rendering work elsewhere can push a timing-fragile arm over. So it was established rather than assumed, and the flake is real and worth owning rather than re-running past.

## Measured

**Mechanism, ruled out first.** The spec loads `test/playwright/component/apps/empty-viewport`, whose `app.mjs` imports exactly one module: `src/container/Viewport.mjs`. There is **no import path** from that page to `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`, the only `src/` file #18214 touches. In-process coupling is therefore impossible, not merely unlikely.

**Rate, armed serially** (single arm, `-g`, one run per process):

| tree | failures |
|---|---|
| `agent/18169-engine-recreate-default` | **1 / 8** |
| `origin/dev` | **0 / 8** |

Eight runs cannot separate 0% from 12%, and I am not claiming it does. What the two together do establish is that the arm fails on a tree where the change under test cannot reach it — which is the question that mattered.

Worth recording against the "it is pre-existing" reflex: **#18214 was the only failing run in the last 25 workflow runs**, with `dev` green at 14:53 and 14:28. That pattern points at the branch, and it is why the import-path check was needed rather than a shrug. At a ~12% rate, 24 consecutive green runs has probability ≈ 0.88²⁴ ≈ 4.6% — low enough that the flake is plausibly **load-dependent** and higher under CI parallelism than in a single-arm local run.

## The Problem

The arm waits for the reopened menu to carry a resolved-zone class:

```javascript
await expect.poll(async () => page.evaluate(id => {
    const node = document.getElementById(id);

    return node ? [...node.classList].find(cls => cls.startsWith('neo-aligned-')) ?? '' : '';
}, menuId)).toMatch(/^neo-aligned-/);
```

Then reads `animationName` **once**, outside any poll:

```javascript
const animationName = await page.evaluate(
    id => getComputedStyle(document.getElementById(id)).animationName, menuId
);

expect(animationName).not.toBe('none')
```

The poll gates on the **alignment** class and the assertion reads the **animation**. Those are two different settlements. `neo-aligned-*` lands when the align pass resolves a zone; `animationName` becomes non-`none` when the entrance class is applied and the stylesheet matches. Nothing here establishes that the second has happened when the first has — so the single read can land in the window between them and see `none`.

The arm's own comments show the author already fought two adjacent races here (a locator count that a focus-driven dismissal can invalidate, and a `.not.toBeNull()` that `undefined` satisfies). This is the third instance of the same shape, one settlement over.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — the animation read is inside a poll, or gated on a signal that is true only after the entrance class has applied. The alignment class must not be used as a proxy for it.
- [ ] **AC-2** — red-first, and **not** by waiting for the flake: with the entrance class suppressed the arm fails deterministically, proving the assertion still witnesses the animation rather than merely surviving.
- [ ] **AC-3** — 30 serial repeats of this arm on the fixed spec, zero failures. The current arm is measured at 1/8, so the count has to be large enough to mean something.
- [ ] **AC-4** — the two adjacent races the comments already describe stay guarded; this must not fix the third by loosening the first two.
- [ ] **AC-5** — the rest of `SpawnAnimation.spec.mjs` stays green, and the full `components` job passes at exact head.

## Out of Scope

- **The spawn animation itself.** Nothing here suggests the feature is broken — the arm sees `none` because it reads too early, not because the entrance failed to arm.
- **A retry or `test.retry` annotation.** That hides the arm's inability to observe its own subject, which is the defect.
- Other intermittents in the `components` job. #18003 was the same *class* on a different subject and is closed; if a pattern is forming across specs, that is its own lane.

## Avoided Traps

- **Calling it "pre-existing" on a relay.** A flake with no named cause and no dated commit is an unowned red that trains the team to re-run. The cause here is named: a poll on one settlement guarding an assertion about another.
- **Blaming the change under test because the branch was the only red run.** The 25-run pattern genuinely pointed at #18214; the import-path check is what settled it, and no amount of re-running would have.

- PR #18214 — where it surfaced; unrelated to its diff

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-03T15:51:19Z

## My diagnosis in this ticket is wrong. The node is absent, not misaligned.

I filed this naming the cause as a poll that gates on one settlement and asserts about another. That defect is **real** and I fixed it. It is **not** what makes the arm flake, and AC-3 proves it: 30 serial repeats of the fixed arm gave **1 failure**, not zero.

So the mechanism was proved red-first and is still only a candidate — exactly the trap of treating a red-first mutation as a cure.

### What actually fails

Captured at the failure rather than reasoned about. The arm reddens at the **alignment** poll (`:201`), not at the animation read I rewrote, and the poll's `''` was hiding which of two states it meant:

```
DIAG-ALIGN {"nodePresent":false,"classes":null,"inDom":false,"menuCount":0}
```

**The reopened menu is not in the DOM at all.** Not unaligned — absent. `document.querySelectorAll('.neo-menu-list').length` is `0`.

That is why `''` was uninformative: the poll returned the same empty string for *node absent* and for *node present but unaligned*, and those are different failures with different causes. A poll whose sentinel collapses two states cannot tell you which one you are in.

### The likely mechanism, and it is in the arm's own comment

> *"the reopened menu takes focus, and a locator count that momentarily matches can be followed by a focus-driven dismissal before the read lands"*

The author already met this hazard and responded by observing the subject **id** instead of the `.neo-menu-list` locator. That changes what is read; it does not stop the dismissal. So the sequence is:

1. `hidden: false` — the menu remounts
2. it takes focus
3. a focus-driven dismissal closes it again
4. the alignment poll finds no node, and times out on `''`

`DomAccess.mjs:305` carries a related note — a hidden menu *"is removed from the DOM and remounts as a fresh element, so it comes back classless while `_aligns` still reports the same zone"* — which is the guard that exists **because** this remount path is fragile. Whether the dismissal here is legitimate behaviour the arm must accommodate, or a defect in the reopen path, is the open question and I am not guessing at it.

### What changes

**The fix I committed stays, and it is not the flake fix.** It polls the entrance on its own state and matches positively against the four keyframe names rather than `not.toBe('none')`, which any string satisfies. Both are genuine improvements to an arm that could pass while measuring the wrong settlement — and neither cures the absent node. Landing it as `Refs`, never `Resolves`.

**ACs revised, because two of mine were written against the wrong cause:**

- [ ] **AC-1** — *revised.* The alignment poll must distinguish **node absent** from **node present but unaligned**. The current sentinel returns `''` for both, which is what made three of my diagnostic passes read as an alignment problem.
- [ ] **AC-2** — *unchanged and already met by the committed fix*: with only the entrance class stripped and alignment left intact, the animation poll fails `Expected pattern: /^neo-menu-spawn-from-…/ · Received "none"` under its own named message. That proves the assertion witnesses the animation specifically. It says nothing about the flake.
- [ ] **AC-3** — *unchanged and NOT met.* 1 failure in 30 on the fixed arm. This is the AC that caught my wrong diagnosis and it stays as written.
- [ ] **AC-6** — *new.* Establish whether the post-reopen dismissal is legitimate. If it is, the arm must wait for the menu to settle **open** before reading anything off it. If it is not, this ticket splits and the engine half gets its own.

### Why this is recorded rather than quietly re-scoped

The measurements that led me wrong are worth more than the correction. I had a plausible mechanism, proved it red-first, and would have closed this ticket on it — with the flake still live at 1-in-30 and a green PR body saying otherwise. AC-3 is the only reason that did not happen, and I set it at 30 repeats because the arm measured 1-in-8. A smaller number would have passed.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-04T14:46:01Z

## AC-6 answered on the factual half — and the focus story this arm has carried since it was written is **falsified**

Measured on `origin/dev@5a7cb7d1f1`, serial, single worker. Diagnosis only; nothing committed.

### The rate is worse than recorded, not better

**3 failures in 30** on the *fixed* arm, and a later run gave 1 in 30 and another 3 in 30. AC-3 said 1-in-30 when I wrote it; it is not a fluke I can wait out. Every failure is the alignment poll timing out the full 5000 ms with the sentinel reading `"absent"` — the sentinel I added is doing exactly the job it was added for.

### The trajectory, which a poll could never show

A `MutationObserver` on the subject id across the reopen window, three separate failures:

```
275ms before-reopen  count=0 present=false
280ms ADDED          count=1 present=true
326ms REMOVED        count=0 present=false
```
```
380ms before-reopen → 386ms ADDED → 430ms REMOVED
281ms before-reopen → 291ms ADDED → 326ms REMOVED
```

**The menu does remount** — 5–10 ms after `hidden: false` — and is removed **35–46 ms later**, then never returns. So "absent" was never "it did not come back". It came back and something took it away, which is a different defect with a different owner.

### The focus hypothesis is dead

The arm's own comment, and my earlier reasoning, blamed a focus-driven dismissal:

> *"the reopened menu takes focus, and a locator count that momentarily matches can be followed by a focus-driven dismissal before the read lands"*

I logged `focusin` and `focusout` on `document` in the capture phase for the whole window. **Zero focus events fired.** Not one, on any failing run. No focus transition accompanies or precedes the removal.

One caveat I will not hide: removing a focused element can move focus without firing an event, so this rules out a focus change *causing* the removal, not focus loss *resulting* from it. The ordering carries the argument — a cause would have to precede its effect, and nothing precedes it.

### What the instance says after the removal

Post-mortem read of `['hidden', 'mounted', 'menuFocus', 'floating', 'isRoot']` on the failing run:

```
[true, false, false, true, true]
```

**`hidden` is `true`** — after the test set it to `false`. The menu was re-*hidden*, not merely unmounted. With `menuFocus: false` on a floating root, `afterSetMenuFocus` → `unmount()` is the shape that fits.

`List#unmount()` writes `_menuFocus = false` **silently**, so that write is a consequence and cannot be the cause. Nothing in `src/menu/**` assigns `hidden` at all, so the `hidden: true` arrives from `super.unmount()` or above.

### What is established, and what is not

**Established:** the node mounts and is removed ~40 ms later; the instance ends `hidden: true, mounted: false, menuFocus: false`; no DOM focus event occurs in the window.

**Not established:** what writes `menuFocus = false`. `onFocusLeave` is its only non-silent writer, and no focus event fired — so either it is reached without one, or something else drives the unmount. My leading candidate is the *first* dismissal's focus-leave landing asynchronously after the reopen has already mounted, which would explain the absence of a new event. **I am not asserting that.** It needs worker-side instrumentation on `menuFocus` transitions, which is where this goes next.

### Disposition

**AC-6 splits, per its own wording.** The dismissal is not the arm accommodating legitimate behaviour: a floating menu that a consumer un-hides, which mounts and re-hides itself 40 ms later with no user interaction and no focus event, is an engine defect — a user would see it flash. The engine half needs its own ticket once the `menuFocus` writer is named; filing it now would put a mechanism in a body I have not measured, which is the mistake this ticket already corrected once.

This ticket keeps AC-3, still unmet, and now owns a reproduction that names the trajectory instead of a symptom.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-04T14:49:43Z

## Retracting my last comment's central claim: the focus hypothesis is NOT dead. It is the mechanism, and I now have it.

Twelve minutes ago I wrote *"The focus hypothesis is dead — zero focus events fired."* **That was wrong**, and it was wrong for the reason this ticket keeps teaching: I read silence from an instrument that could not see the property.

I listened for `focusin`/`focusout` on `document` in the **main realm**. The focus lifecycle that matters runs in the **app worker**, through Neo's own focus-path delivery. My listener was structurally incapable of witnessing it, and I reported its silence as absence. Same class as the `''` sentinel this ticket already corrected once, and as the `.not.toBeNull()` before that. Third time in one file.

### The mechanism, measured

I instrumented `menuFocus` transitions, `onFocusLeave` and `unmount` **worker-side**, on the instance, read back through `getConfigs`. **7 failures in 60 repeats, and all 7 produced a byte-identical trail:**

```
setMenuFocus undefined->false              ← construction
setMenuFocus false->true                   ← the reopened menu mounts and takes focus
onFocusLeave related=false oldPathLen=7    ← a focus LEAVE arrives, with no relatedTarget
setMenuFocus true->false                   ← List.mjs:531 — the `!data.relatedTarget` branch
unmount                                    ← afterSetMenuFocus unmounts the floating root
```

Not one variant across seven failures. This is deterministic once the window opens, not a grab-bag of timings.

So the chain is:

1. `hidden: false` remounts the menu; it takes focus and `menuFocus` goes **true**.
2. A focus **leave** lands with `relatedTarget` falsy and a 7-entry `oldPath`.
3. `onFocusLeave` takes its first branch — `if (!data.relatedTarget || …)` — and writes `menuFocus = false`.
4. `afterSetMenuFocus(false)` on a floating root calls `unmount()`.
5. The node is removed ~40 ms after mount and the instance settles `hidden: true`.

The leave carries an `oldPath` of 7, so focus genuinely *was* somewhere and left. Nothing in the test moves focus after the reopen. The strong reading is that this leave belongs to the **first** dismissal — it is delivered asynchronously and lands after the reopen has already mounted and armed `menuFocus`, so a stale leave from one lifecycle unmounts the *next* instance. That is consistent with my main-realm listener seeing nothing: the DOM event fired before the reopen, and therefore before the listener existed.

I am stating that last step as the strong reading, not as measured. What is measured is steps 1–5.

### A Heisenbug worth recording

My first worker-side probe captured `new Error().stack` on every transition and the flake vanished entirely: **30/30 green**. Removing the stack capture and keeping cheap string pushes brought it back at **7/60**. The race window is narrow enough that per-transition stack construction closes it — which is corroboration for an ordering race rather than a logic error, and a warning to anyone who instruments this next.

### Disposition

**AC-6 is answered and the split it calls for is now justified**, because the mechanism is measured rather than guessed. A floating menu that a consumer un-hides, which mounts and then unmounts itself because a leave from the previous lifecycle applied to the new one, is an engine defect — a user sees it flash. Filing the engine half next, with this trail as its evidence.

This ticket keeps AC-3 and now owns a named cause instead of a symptom.

## All five ACs verified on current `dev` — this shipped in #18219 and the ticket never closed

The fix landed 2026-09-03 as `82068064db`, *"test(menu): the spawn re-arm arm measures the entrance, and names what is absent"*, merged via PR #18219. **That PR's body carries no `Resolves` line**, so nothing closed this ticket — the work has been done for five days while the ticket read as open. Recording the evidence rather than closing on the commit title.

| AC | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **AC-1** — the animation read is inside a poll, not proxied by the alignment class | met | `SpawnAnimation.spec.mjs:231-241` polls `animationName` on its own state. Stronger than asked: it matches **positively** against `/^neo-menu-spawn-from-(top\|bottom\|left\|right)$/` rather than `not.toBe('none')`, which any string satisfies — including a `neo-aligned-` class the stylesheet has no rule for |
| **AC-2** — red-first by suppressing the entrance, **not** by waiting for the flake | met | Ran it just now. Created the subject with `animateSpawn: false` and the arm failed **deterministically**, 3/3: `Expected pattern: /^neo-menu-spawn-from-(top\|bottom\|left\|right)$/` / `Received string: "none"`. So the assertion witnesses the animation rather than merely surviving. Spec restored to `animateSpawn: true`; working tree clean |
| **AC-3** — 30 serial repeats, zero failures | met | `--repeat-each=30 --workers=1` on the re-arm arm: **30 passed (29.4s)** |
| **AC-4** — the two adjacent races stay guarded | met | Both intact and still commented at their sites: the locator-count race (`:189-192`, observed on the subject id rather than `.neo-menu-list`, because the reopened menu takes focus and a momentarily-matching count can be followed by a focus-driven dismissal) and the `absent`-vs-`unaligned` sentinel (`:198-210`, where the previous `''` returned the same value for both). Neither was loosened to fix the third |
| **AC-5** — the rest of the spec stays green | met | Full `SpawnAnimation.spec.mjs` on the restored tree: **8 passed** |

**On AC-2's method, because it is the AC that matters most here.** The ticket explicitly forbade proving red-first by waiting for the 1-in-8 flake, and it was right to: a flake reproduction shows the arm *can* fail, never that it fails *for the AC's reason*. Suppressing the entrance class produces the exact string the defect produced — `none` — from a cause I chose, which is the difference between a control and a coincidence.

**What this ticket bought, stated as the class rather than the instance.** The arm polled the **alignment** settlement and asserted on the **animation** settlement. `List.scss` keys the entrance on two classes at once — `.neo-animate-spawn` and a specific `.neo-aligned-*` — so alignment landing is necessary and not sufficient. A poll on one settlement gating an assertion on another is the shape; the file's own comments record that this was the **third** instance of it in the same arm, after a locator count and a `.not.toBeNull()` that `undefined` satisfies.

Nothing outstanding. Closing as completed.
